notable_anecdotes: The Holy Trinity entrance test failure: the priest asked 'Name the three persons of God' and the author replied 'Jesus, Mary, Joseph' -- an honest mistake that became the origin story of his deeper Catholic formation.

Miggy Panganiban Sandejas (5 years old, the author's grandson) gifting JP II a crayola-colored caricature titled 'Viva il Papa!' and a salakot that the Pope gamely tried on -- to the crowd's applause.
JP II breaking security protocols to wade into 1,500 dancing schoolchildren, with President Ramos gamely following -- one of the most humanizing moments in any papal visit to the Philippines.

Archbishop Morelos's rehearsal prophecy ('You will be president someday') and the author's counter-prophecy ('You will be pope') -- neither came true, but 1995 brought both the SC appointment and the PCL membership instead.

one_paragraph_summary: On the occasion of JP II's beatification, Panganiban reminisces about his two main encounters with the Pope. First, JP II's January 12-16, 1995 pastoral visit to Manila: the author served on the Arrival and Departure Committee under Ambassador Tita de Villa; Archbishop Morelos played the Pope in rehearsals (prophesying the author would be president) while the author played President Ramos (counter-prophesying Morelos would be pope -- neither came true). At the actual arrival, the author's 5-year-old grandson Miggy gifted JP II a crayola 'Viva il Papa!' caricature and a salakot the Pope gamely tried on; JP II then broke security to wade into 1,500 dancing schoolchildren, with Ramos gamely following. Second, JP II's appointment of the author to the Pontifical Council for the Laity (PCL) for the 1996-2001 term -- the only Filipino among 30 Catholic leaders from around the world, meeting annually in the Vatican. The irony: the author had been denied admission to a Catholic university because he couldn't name the three persons of the Holy Trinity ('Jesus, Mary, Joseph' was his answer) -- yet became a PCL adviser to the Holy Father 'by some miracle and as pure gift from God.' The column also updates the Manila Cathedral-Basilica rehabilitation: JP II elevated it to a basilica in 1981; Cardinal Rosales's concern about structural deterioration led to the Manila Cathedral-Basilica Foundation (author as president, Cardinal Rosales as chair, Marixi Prieto as VP); the seven bells were lowered from the belfry and replaced with a P5 million electronic carillon (donated by Alberto and Sylvia Lina); the complete rehabilitation needs about P200 million.
